This violates the project's 'no incorrect silent fallbacks / fail loudly' rule. Using `log_model(...).registered_model_version` eliminates both the race and the bogus fallback in one line.
evidence: lines 124-131 call `mlflow.pyfunc.log_model(...)` but ignore its return; lines 135-140: `versions = search_versions(client, uc_model_name); if versions: latest_version = max(versions, key=lambda v: int(v.version)).version else: latest_version = "1"`; line 152 feeds `int(latest_version)` straight into the live endpoint. `ModelInfo.registered_model_version` exists in installed mlflow 3.10.0.

title: Unreachable `if errors:` warning branch in validate_deploy (always-False after the raise)
description: In `validate_deploy`, the block `if errors or test_quote_errors: ... raise DeployError(...)` (lines 319-330) raises whenever either error list is non-empty. Execution only continues past line 330 when BOTH `errors` and `test_quote_errors` are empty. The very next statement is `if errors: logger.warning("validation_failed", error_count=len(errors))` (lines 332-333) with an `else: logger.info("validation_passed")`. Because `errors` is provably empty at this point, the `if errors:` condition is always False and the `logger.warning(...)` on line 333 is unreachable dead code. Only the `else` branch (line 335, `validation_passed`) can ever run. This is a stale leftover from before `test_quote_errors` was folded into the line-319 guard: the function used to raise on `errors` alone, so this trailing `if errors:` once made sense; now it cannot. The entire 332-335 block reduces to a single `logger.info("validation_passed")`.
evidence: Line 319 guard: `if errors or test_quote_errors:` -> raises on line 326. Reaching line 332 implies `not (errors or test_quote_errors)`, i.e. `errors == []`. Therefore `if errors:` at line 332 is always False; line 333 (`error_count=len(errors)`) never executes. Grep confirms the only `error_count=` + `validation_failed` reference in the codebase is this dead line itself, and no test asserts this warning fires (only `validation_passed` is reachable). Not covered by the three known findings (validate-time scoring w/o artifact_paths; SIMP-12 Decimal dedup; BUG-1 double-scoring).
est_reduction: ~3 LOC (collapse lines 332-335 to a single `logger.info("validation_passed")`)
behavior_preservation: Removing the unreachable warning branch and keeping only `logger.info("validation_passed")` is exactly equivalent: the deleted code path is provably never taken, so no observable behavior (logs, return value, raises) changes for any input.

title: validate_deploy parses every test-quote file twice (pre-check load_test_quote_file + score_test_quotes re-parse)
description: Within a single `validate_deploy` call, each `*.json` in `test_quotes_dir` is JSON-parsed and case-validated twice. First, the missing-required-column pre-check loop (lines 296-309) calls `load_test_quote_file(jf)` -> `_load_test_quote_cases` -> `json.loads(read_user_text(path))` + `_parse_test_quote_case` per row. Immediately after, `score_test_quotes(resolved, tq_dir)` (line 312) re-globs the same directory and re-parses every file via `_load_test_quote_cases` (line 371). The file read, JSON decode, and full golden-row validation are therefore performed twice per file per `validate_deploy`. The pre-check needs the parsed rows only to diff column names against `input_schema`; `score_test_quotes` already parses the identical cases and could supply them (or the pre-check could be folded into the scoring loop). This is distinct from the known BUG-1, which concerns `handle_deploy` running the full scoring pass (score_graph) twice across `validate_deploy`+`handle_deploy`; here the duplicated work is the parse/validation inside `validate_deploy` itself.
evidence: load_test_quote_file (line 116) -> `_load_test_quote_cases` (line 102) -> `json.loads(read_user_text(path))`. score_test_quotes (line 371) -> `_load_test_quote_cases(jf)` on the same files from the same `sorted(tq_dir.glob("*.json"))`. validate_deploy invokes both: pre-check loop at 296-309 and `score_test_quotes(resolved, tq_dir)` at 312. No caching of parsed cases between the two passes.
est_reduction: ~10 LOC and one JSON parse + validation per test-quote file per validate_deploy (fold the column pre-check into the scoring loop, or have the scorer return/accept already-parsed cases)
behavior_preservation: Parsing once and reusing the cases yields identical error detection: the same missing-column messages and the same scoring/expected-output errors are produced; only the redundant second parse is removed. Parse errors are still surfaced (currently as a parse error in the pre-check; consolidating must keep the same 'could not parse' message).

title: _resolve_path has a dead `exists()` branch; both arms return the identical value
description: After computing `pipeline_abs = (pipeline_dir / p).resolve()`, the function does `if pipeline_abs.exists(): return pipeline_abs` immediately followed by `return pipeline_abs`. Both branches return the exact same object, so the `pipeline_abs.exists()` check is dead — it has no observable effect and performs an unnecessary stat() syscall. The whole tail can be collapsed to a single `return pipeline_abs`. The surrounding docstring (lines 213-225) compounds the confusion: it describes a multi-step 'Resolution order' that prefers CWD when both exist ('The old code preferred CWD'), but the current code never consults CWD at all — relative paths are unconditionally resolved against `pipeline_dir`. The test `test_collect_artifacts_resolves_against_pipeline_dir_not_cwd` confirms the actual (single-path) behavior, and its sibling docstring at tests/test_deploy_config_and_bundle.py:13/247 still describes the obsolete 'tries CWD first' contract.
est_reduction: ~4 lines of body collapsed to 1; plus an opportunity to fix the now-inaccurate docstring (no behavior change).
behavior_preservation: Collapsing the two-arm tail to a single `return pipeline_abs` is exactly behavior-preserving: both arms already return the same `Path`. Removing the `.exists()` call only drops a redundant filesystem stat with no effect on the returned value (missing files are still caught downstream by `_check_exists`).

title: _verify_static_source_schema treats a bare `schema` key as a schema declaration the read adapter never honors, causing a no-op file read
description: `has_schema_declaration` (lines 173-175) gates the verification read on the presence of any of `schema_overrides`, `dtypes`, `column_dtypes`, or `schema`. For the first three, the read is meaningful: `read_data_source` -> `build_data_source_adapter` -> `_schema_overrides_from_config` (src/haute/_io.py:127-138) recognizes exactly `schema_overrides`/`dtypes`/`column_dtypes` and runs `_validate_declared_schema` during the read, so declared-dtype drift is enforced at the deploy boundary. But `_schema_overrides_from_config` does NOT recognize a bare `schema` key. So a static dataSource whose config carries only `schema` (and no `expected_columns`, no schema_overrides/dtypes/column_dtypes) passes the gate, performs a full `read_data_source(...).collect_schema()` whose `actual` is then discarded (the `if expected and ...` block at line 199 is skipped because `expected` is falsy), and validates nothing. The result is wasted deploy-time I/O plus a false impression that the `schema` declaration is being enforced, when it is silently ignored. This is an inconsistency between the gate's recognized keys and the adapter's recognized keys.
evidence:
Gate at lines 173-176:
    has_schema_declaration = any(
        key in config for key in ("schema_overrides", "dtypes", "column_dtypes", "schema")
    )
    if not expected and not has_schema_declaration:
        return
Adapter recognition at src/haute/_io.py:127-138 (`_schema_overrides_from_config`) keys on only `schema_overrides`/`dtypes`/`column_dtypes` — `schema` is absent. With config={'schema': {...}} and no expected_columns: line 176 does not early-return, lines 183-189 read+compute `actual`, line 199 `if expected and ...` is False, function returns having enforced nothing.

title: liveSwitch deploy pruning MAPPED (input_scenario_map) path silently selects the wrong live branch when two upstream labels collide under _sanitize_func_name (order-dependent, no ambiguity guard)
description: When a liveSwitch node DOES have an input_scenario_map with a 'live' entry, _live_only_edges resolves the live edge by scanning the switch's incoming edges and taking the FIRST whose source label sanitizes to live_input_name (lines 59-64), then `break`s. The guard at lines 65-69 only raises when NO edge matches. It does NOT detect the case where TWO distinct upstream source nodes have labels that collide under _sanitize_func_name (e.g. 'Live Source' and 'Live-Source' both -> 'Live_Source', since sanitize maps both space and hyphen to '_'). In that case both edges 'match' live_input_name; whichever edge is listed first in graph.edges wins, the other live-candidate is dropped, and prune_for_deploy returns normally with NO error. The deployed scoring path therefore depends on edge ordering and can keep the WRONG upstream branch. This is the inverse of the already-known fallback finding: the known finding (bucket 'known', verdict refuted) asserts the mapped path is the safe one that 'raises on no-match/collision, unlike the fallback' — this finding shows the mapped path is ALSO silently order-dependent on COLLISION (it only raises on no-match, not on ambiguous-match). It is also distinct from the codegen B3 finding, which concerns two input_scenario_map keys both mapped to 'live' (duplicate map VALUES); here the map has a single 'live' key but two SOURCE LABELS collide after sanitization.
evidence: Executed repro (temp script, project root sandboxed, then deleted). Graph: nodes a='Live Source'(dataSource), b='Live-Source'(dataSource) [both sanitize to 'Live_Source'], switch=liveSwitch config={input_scenario_map:{'Live_Source':'live','Other':'batch'}, inputs:['Live_Source','Other']}, output. Edges to switch ordered (a,b) vs (b,a). prune_for_deploy(graph,'output') returned with NO exception in both cases; surviving switch parent = {'a'} for order (a,b) and {'b'} for order (b,a). So the kept live branch flips with edge order and exactly one colliding source is silently chosen. Code trace: line 60 `if e.target == sid`; line 62 `if _sanitize_func_name(src_label) == live_input_name`; line 63 sets switch_live_source[sid]=e.source; line 64 `break` -> first-match-wins; the line 65 `if sid not in switch_live_source` guard never fires because a (colliding) match was found.

title: Duplicated 'first incoming edge whose sanitized source label matches live_input_name' scan in both branches of _live_only_edges
description: The fallback branch (lines 52-57) and the mapped branch (lines 59-64) contain a verbatim-identical edge-scan loop: `for e in edges: if e.target == sid: src_label = node_map[e.source].data.label; if _sanitize_func_name(src_label) == live_input_name: switch_live_source[sid] = e.source; break`. The only difference is the surrounding guard (fallback gates on `if live_input_name:` and never raises; mapped raises at 65-69 when unmatched). Extracting the shared loop into a single helper, e.g. `_first_source_matching_label(edges, sid, node_map, live_input_name) -> str | None`, and having each branch call it (mapped raising on None, fallback leaving switch_live_source unset on None) removes the duplication and makes the live-resolution rule single-sourced, which also makes the collision behavior in the related bug finding visible in one place.
evidence: Lines 52-57 and 59-64 are character-for-character the same loop body apart from indentation; both iterate `edges`, filter `e.target == sid`, sanitize `node_map[e.source].data.label`, compare to `live_input_name`, assign `switch_live_source[sid]`, and `break`.
est_reduction: ~8 lines
behavior_preservation: Behavior-preserving: a shared helper iterates `edges` in the same order and returns the same first match (or None); mapped path raises on None exactly as today (lines 65-69), fallback path leaves switch_live_source[sid] unset on None exactly as today. No change to which edges survive.

title: executeSink is the only data endpoint that skips runtime response validation, casting the raw wire body to SinkResponse
description: Every other endpoint in this file pipes the parsed JSON through a runtime guard before returning (loadPipeline -> parsePipelineResponse, previewNode -> parsePreviewNodeResponse, savePipeline -> parseSavePipelineResponse, traceCell -> parseTraceResponse, createSubmodel -> parseSubmodelCreateResponse). executeSink instead does `return post(...)` with no `.then(parseSinkResponse)` and the function signature `Promise<SinkResponse>` forces an unchecked structural cast of whatever `res.json()` returned. There is no parseSinkResponse guard anywhere in src/types/guards.ts, and executeSink is the single data-returning endpoint absent from both client.contract.test.ts (which exercises malformed-200 rejection for the others) and from any response-shape assertion in client.test.ts (its three tests only assert the outgoing request body). This breaks the file's own invariant that backend responses fail loudly at the boundary (per CLAUDE.md: 'code should be allowed to fail loudly... far superior to a fallback which is incorrect and hard to notice'). The downstream consumer SinkEditor.tsx:47-48 reads `data.status || 'ok'` and `data.message || 'Written successfully'`, so a malformed/garbage payload is silently masked by `||` fallbacks rather than surfaced — the exact 'incorrect and hard to notice' situation the codebase guards against. Practical blast radius is limited because the consumer only touches two optional string fields with fallbacks, hence not a crash, but row_count/path/format are never validated and any future consumer would trust an unverified shape.
evidence: client.ts:571-580 `return post("/api/pipeline/sink", {...}, { signal, timeout })` with no parse step, vs client.ts:550 `post<unknown>("/api/pipeline/trace", body, ...).then(parseTraceResponse)`. SinkResponse defined types.ts:202-208 (status/message/row_count/path/format). No `parseSinkResponse` symbol exists (grep across frontend). Consumer SinkEditor.tsx:47-49 masks with `data.status || 'ok'` / `data.message || 'Written successfully'`.
behavior_preservation: For well-formed backend responses, adding a parseSinkResponse guard returns the same object and is fully behavior-preserving; it only changes behavior for malformed payloads (which currently slip through with silent `||` fallbacks) by making them fail loudly, matching the rest of the client.

title: Chart tab silently coerces/drops non-finite series values while Statistics tab throws into the ErrorBoundary
description: toQuoteRow reads each series value with Number(row[col] ?? 0). The ?? only catches null/undefined, so a genuinely-null cell becomes a fabricated 0 plotted on the chart, and a non-numeric value (e.g. the string 'n/a') becomes NaN. The Chart render path then propagates NaN into SVG geometry with no user-facing signal, whereas the Statistics tab feeds the exact same rows to computeScenarioStatsBySeries, whose readFiniteNumber THROWS on null/empty/non-finite. The result: identical preview data renders a silently-wrong/broken chart in the Chart tab but trips the panel's ErrorBoundary (App.tsx:647, replacing the whole preview with the error fallback) the instant the user switches to the Statistics tab. This is an inconsistent, silent-wrongness path that contradicts the project's 'fail loudly, no incorrect fallbacks' guidance.
evidence: Line 50: vals[col] = Number(row[col] ?? 0)  // null -> 0 (silent fake value); 'abc' -> NaN. buildSeriesScale line 94: const v = r.values[column] ?? 0 (NaN ?? 0 === NaN, not caught) -> NaN never updates vMin/vMax. SeriesLine line 265: `...${yScale(r.values[column] ?? 0).toFixed(1)}` and lines 274-277 cx/cy=yScale(NaN) -> 'NaN' path segment + circle at NaN (invisible/broken) with no warning. Contrast optimiserScenarioStats.ts readFiniteNumber (line 31-38) which throws Error('Expected finite numeric value...') for the same null/'abc' cell; computeScenarioStatsBySeries is called from line 528-536 inside a useMemo, so the throw during render hits ErrorBoundary name="NodePreview" at App.tsx:647. Same data -> silent broken chart vs hard error fallback depending only on which tab is active.
behavior_preservation: n/a

title: Duplicated quote-ID truncation with inconsistent threshold and ellipsis glyph
description: The same 'truncate the current quote id for display' behaviour is hand-rolled twice with different limits and different ellipsis characters: the nav header truncates at length > 12 to slice(0,10) + ASCII '...', while the sidebar truncates at length > 14 to slice(0,12) + Unicode '…'. A single shared helper (e.g. truncateMiddle/truncateEnd(id, n)) would remove the duplication and the visual inconsistency where the two displays of one id can disagree on whether/how it is shortened.
evidence: Line 599: {currentQuoteId.length > 12 ? currentQuoteId.slice(0, 10) + "..." : currentQuoteId}. Lines 716-718: {currentQuoteId.length > 14 ? currentQuoteId.slice(0, 12) + "…" : currentQuoteId}. Different cutoff (12 vs 14), different prefix length (10 vs 12), different ellipsis ('...' vs '…').
est_reduction: ~4 lines plus removal of inconsistency
behavior_preservation: Behaviour-preserving only if both call sites are unified to one rule; choosing one threshold/glyph is a deliberate, tiny visual normalisation.

title: allSeriesKey = JSON.stringify(allSeries) recomputed every render despite single effect-only use
description: allSeriesKey is computed unconditionally on every render via JSON.stringify, but its sole consumer is the dependency array of the checked-series sync effect (lines 454-457, with exhaustive-deps disabled). Since allSeries is already a memoized stable reference (lines 424-431), the effect could simply depend on allSeries directly (set membership re-syncs only when the memo identity changes), removing both the per-render stringify and the eslint-disable. If a value-based key is genuinely desired it should be wrapped in useMemo keyed on allSeries.
evidence: Line 434: const allSeriesKey = JSON.stringify(allSeries) — runs on every render. Lines 454-457: useEffect(() => { setCheckedSeries(new Set(allSeries)) /* eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps */ }, [allSeriesKey]). allSeries memoized at 424-431 on [objectiveCol, constraintCols], so its reference already changes iff the series list changes.
est_reduction: 1 line + 1 eslint-disable removed, plus a per-render JSON.stringify
behavior_preservation: Depending on allSeries identity instead of its JSON string preserves behaviour because allSeries is memoized and only re-created when the series list changes; the resulting Set re-sync timing is identical.

title: Regex fallback silently drops # haute:preserve-start/end blocks, causing data loss on the next save
description: fallback_parse builds the returned PipelineGraph without ever extracting preserved blocks. The healthy parser (parser.py:165-176) calls `_extract_preserved_blocks(source)` and passes `preserved_blocks=...` to PipelineGraph; the fallback omits this entirely. `PipelineGraph.preserved_blocks` defaults to `[]` (_types.py:652), so any code the user fenced with `# haute:preserve-start` / `# haute:preserve-end` is absent from the recovered graph. When the GUI later saves the (still syntactically-broken-on-disk) file, codegen reads `graph.preserved_blocks` (codegen.py:932/1243) and emits them via `_emit_preserved_blocks` (codegen.py:728-729); because the parser never populated them, the preserved code is permanently dropped from the regenerated file. `_extract_preserved_blocks` is pure line-scanning (no AST), so it works on broken source and could be called here. This is the same data-loss-on-save failure mode as the known submodel finding, but a distinct artifact (preserved blocks).
evidence: fallback_parse return omits preserved_blocks=; PipelineGraph.preserved_blocks default_factory=list (_types.py:652); codegen.py:932 `all_preserved = ... graph.preserved_blocks`; codegen.py:728-729 emits them. _extract_preserved_blocks (_ast_helpers.py:520-548) is text-only and import-available in this module's _ast_helpers import group.

title: Unreachable config-inferred-type branch and unused recovered_type
description: Inside the `config_kwarg` recovery block, `loaded_config, recovered_type = recovered` is unpacked, then `if not block['explicit_node_type']: node_type = recovered_type`. `block['explicit_node_type']` is set in _find_function_blocks (line 563) to `DECORATOR_TO_NODE_TYPE[decorator_method]`, and `decorator_method` is filtered to be a key of that dict (line 522). Every value in DECORATOR_TO_NODE_TYPE is a non-empty NodeType StrEnum member (all truthy). Therefore `not block['explicit_node_type']` is always False, lines 690-691 never execute, and `recovered_type` is never used. node_type was already initialised to the same explicit_node_type at line 677, so the branch can never change it.
evidence: _find_function_blocks:522 `if decorator_method not in DECORATOR_TO_NODE_TYPE: continue`; line 563 `'explicit_node_type': DECORATOR_TO_NODE_TYPE[decorator_method]`; NodeType members are all non-empty strings (_types.py:32-50). fallback_parse:677 `node_type = block['explicit_node_type']`. So line 690 guard is statically always False.
est_reduction: ~4 lines + simplify unpack to `loaded_config, _ = recovered`
behavior_preservation: Branch is provably unreachable; removing it (and the unused recovered_type) cannot change behavior.

title: _RE_DECORATOR compiled pattern is unused by the parser (only exercised by vestigial tests)
description: `_RE_DECORATOR` is compiled at module load but never referenced anywhere in the production codebase. `_find_function_blocks` locates decorators with `_RE_DECORATOR_ANCHOR` plus `_recover_decorator_text`/`_find_decorated_def`; the full multi-part `_RE_DECORATOR` regex (which truncates args at the first `)` and so could not recover nested-call decorators anyway) is leftover from an earlier implementation. The only references are three tests in tests/test_parser_regex.py (TestRegexPatterns) that exercise the pattern in isolation, pinning a regex the parser no longer uses.
evidence: Grep `_RE_DECORATOR\b` across src/ matches only the definition at _parser_regex.py:42. Cross-file grep shows usages only in tests/test_parser_regex.py:8,248,253,261.
est_reduction: ~6 lines in module + 3 obsolete tests
behavior_preservation: Pattern is never consulted by parser logic; removing it (and its isolation tests) leaves all parsing behavior identical.

title: A wrapped (multi-line) def signature aborts the ENTIRE fallback parse instead of recovering other nodes
description:
_find_decorated_def matches the function header with `re.match(r'def\s+(\w+)\s*\(([^)]*)\)', line)` on a single physical line. A valid but line-wrapped signature (e.g. `def foo(
    a,
    b,
):`) has no closing `)` on the `def` line, so the match is None and the function raises ParseError. fallback_parse calls _find_function_blocks at line 670 without any try/except, so this ParseError propagates out of fallback_parse and aborts recovery of the WHOLE file — every node and edge is lost, not just the one node with the wrapped signature. Because the fallback only runs on files that already failed ast.parse, the realistic trigger is a hand-edited file whose syntax error is elsewhere (e.g. a typo in one body) while an unrelated, perfectly valid node happens to use a multi-line signature. The whole-graph abort defeats the module's stated 'best-effort graph the GUI can render alongside error markers' purpose. (Codegen always emits single-line signatures, so codegen-produced files are unaffected.)
evidence: _find_decorated_def:491 `match = re.match(r"def\s+(\w+)\s*\(([^)]*)\)", line)`; lines 493-497 raise ParseError when match is None. fallback_parse:670 `blocks = _find_function_blocks(source)` is uncaught; _find_function_blocks:526 calls _find_decorated_def. `[^)]*` cannot span the newline of a wrapped signature.

title: Trailing backslash inside a comment on the previous line is misread as a line continuation, skipping a valid top-level connect
description: _has_backslash_continuation_before tests `previous_line.rstrip().endswith('\\')` on the raw text of the previous physical line. A backslash at the end of a comment (e.g. `# see foo \`) or inside a string is NOT a Python line continuation, but this check treats it as one. _is_top_level_statement_anchor returns False when this helper is True (line 181), so a genuine module-level `pipeline.connect(...)` on the following line would be classified as a non-top-level continuation and skipped by _iter_connect_anchor_matches, silently dropping that edge. The helper inspects raw line text rather than code positions (it does not strip comments/strings the way the rest of the module's scanners do), which is the root inconsistency.
evidence: _has_backslash_continuation_before:152 builds previous_line from raw source and returns `.rstrip().endswith('\\')`; _is_top_level_statement_anchor:181 `if wrapper_depth < 0 or _has_backslash_continuation_before(...): return False`. Unlike _skip_string_literal-based scanners elsewhere, no comment/string awareness is applied to the previous line.

title: Fallback path skips _validate_user_contract, so a drifted contract= annotation is not caught at parse time
description: The healthy parser resolves config through _resolve_node_config, which calls _validate_user_contract to cross-check a `contract=` kwarg against the builder-derived contract and raises ContractMismatchError on disagreement (_config_builder.py:434). fallback_parse builds config directly via _build_node_config and merely re-attaches `config['contract'] = decorator_kwargs['contract']` (lines 740-741) with no validation. Contract validation is config-only (it does not require the file to be syntactically whole), so a wrong/drifted contract annotation in a broken file silently survives parse-time. The mismatch is only re-detected later at execution time, diverging from the project's fail-loud-at-parse philosophy that the healthy path implements.
evidence: _resolve_node_config:434 `_validate_user_contract(node_type, config, user_contract, func_name)` raises ContractMismatchError (_config_builder.py:364-372). fallback_parse never calls _resolve_node_config or _validate_user_contract; it only does the unconditional re-attach at 740-741. Compare _config_builder.py:441-442 which attaches AFTER validation.

title: Identical scenario_value_stats / scenario_value_histogram inline parsers duplicated across parseOptimiserSolveResult and parseFrontierSelectResponse
description: The inline object literal that validates `scenario_value_stats` (11 fields: mean/std/min/max/p5/p25/p50/p75/p95/pct_increase/pct_decrease, each via expectNumber) is written out verbatim twice: once in parseOptimiserSolveResult (lines 1480-1490) and once in parseFrontierSelectResponse (lines 1540-1550). The `scenario_value_histogram` inline parser (counts + edges, each `parseArray(... expectNumber ...)`) is likewise duplicated (lines 1492-1497 and 1552-1557). The two copies differ ONLY by the parser-name string literal ('parseOptimiserStatusResponse' vs 'parseFrontierSelectResponse'). Both blocks already operate on a pre-resolved `stats` / `histogram` value produced by optionalNullableObject(...) and both target the same shared wire types (OptimiserScenarioValueStats / OptimiserScenarioValueHistogram in api/types.ts:624-641), so there is no shape difference justifying the copy.
evidence: guards.ts:1480 `mean: expectNumber("parseOptimiserStatusResponse", stats.mean, "field \`scenario_value_stats.mean\`")` is identical to guards.ts:1540 `mean: expectNumber("parseFrontierSelectResponse", stats.mean, "field \`scenario_value_stats.mean\`")` for all 11 fields; the histogram blocks at 1495-1496 and 1555-1556 are identical save the parser name. Both `stats` values come from optionalNullableObject (1457, 1521) and both types alias the same OptimiserScenarioValueStats/OptimiserScenarioValueHistogram interfaces.
est_reduction: ~30 lines (two 11-line stats blocks collapse to one helper call each; two histogram blocks likewise)
behavior_preservation: Extract `parseScenarioValueStats(parser: string, stats: Record<string,unknown>)` and `parseScenarioValueHistogram(parser: string, hist: Record<string,unknown>)` taking the parser-name as a parameter, then call them with the existing literals. Field paths (e.g. `field \`scenario_value_stats.mean\``, `field \`scenario_value_histogram.edges\``) and parser prefixes are reproduced byte-for-byte, so all loud-failure error messages are unchanged. Contract tests assert on `scenario_value_histogram.edges` / `.counts` (guards.contract.test.ts:1026,1039) which the parameterized helper preserves exactly; no behavior change.

title: getGitHistory drops limit=0 via truthiness check, silently using backend default
description: getGitHistory builds the query string with `const params = limit ? `?limit=${limit}` : ""`. Because the guard is a truthiness check rather than `limit !== undefined`, an explicit `limit === 0` is treated the same as omitted: the `?limit=` param is dropped and the backend falls back to its default (git_history's `Query(20, ge=1, le=500)` -> 20). The intent of passing an explicit number is silently ignored for the value 0. This is the only endpoint in the in-scope range that decides param inclusion by truthiness of a numeric value. Impact is minimal in practice: the sole caller (GitPanel.tsx:71) passes 30, and the backend would reject 0 anyway (ge=1), so this changes *which* behavior occurs (default 20 vs a 422) rather than corrupting data. Reported for completeness; the idiomatic fix is `limit !== undefined ? `?limit=${limit}` : ""` (mirroring the `streamingChunkSize !== undefined` pattern used elsewhere in this file).
evidence: client.ts:1163-1168 `export function getGitHistory(limit?: number, options?) { const params = limit ? `?limit=${limit}` : ""; return request(`/api/git/history${params}`, options)... }`. Backend src/haute/routes/git.py:202 `def git_history(limit: int = Query(20, ge=1, le=500))`. With limit=0: `0 ?` is falsy => params="" => backend uses 20. Contrast client.ts:511 which uses `streamingChunkSize !== undefined` to avoid exactly this falsy-zero pitfall.

title: failExploreJob relabels a previous explore report from a DIFFERENT config with the failed job's configHash, causing the panel to show stale cross-config data as the current result
description: On an explore failure, failExploreJob unconditionally preserves the previously cached report (`result: previous?.result ?? null`) but stamps the new entry with the FAILED job's identity (`configHash: job.configHash`, `source: job.source`, `structuralVersion: job.structuralVersion`). When the failure is for a config that differs from the previously successful one, the stored entry now claims an old report belongs to the new config. ExplorePreview's freshness check matches purely on configHash+source (currentCachedResult = cachedResult.configHash === configHash && cachedResult.source === activeSource), so it will surface the stale report (`report = currentCachedResult?.result`) as the result for the new config, with no staleness indicator (explore has no isStale gate, unlike solve/train via useStaleConfigEstimate). The fix is to preserve previous.result only when previous.configHash === job.configHash && previous.source === job.source, else null — matching the solve/train semantics where a failed run for a changed config does not present an old result as current.
evidence: Trace: (1) explore succeeds for config A -> exploreResults[nodeId] = { result: reportA, configHash: A, source: srcA }. (2) user changes config to B, runs explore, it fails -> failExploreJob(nodeId, err, term) with job.configHash = B (job came from startExploreJob with hash B). (3) previous = s.exploreResults[nodeId] = the A entry. (4) nextCached = { result: reportA, configHash: B, source: srcB, structuralVersion: vB, error: err }. (5) In ExplorePreview.tsx:91-95 currentCachedResult matches because configHash===B && source===srcB, so report = reportA and ExploreOverviewPane/DataPreview render reportA's rows/columns as if they are config B's data. The existing test useNodeResultsStore.test.ts:461-480 ('failExploreJob ... without discarding the previous report') exercises exactly this cross-config sequence (h1 -> startExploreJob h2 -> failExploreJob) and asserts cached.result === report while the entry's configHash becomes h2 — it locks in the mislabeling and never asserts configHash, so the bug is currently codified as intended.

title: structuralVersion is threaded through every explore job/result but never read by any consumer — its freshness signal is already fully subsumed by configHash
description: startExploreJob accepts a structuralVersion arg and stores it on ActiveExploreJob; completeExploreJob and failExploreJob copy job.structuralVersion onto CachedExploreResult. No code path ever reads CachedExploreResult.structuralVersion or ActiveExploreJob.structuralVersion to gate freshness (verified by grep across frontend/src). Explore freshness is decided solely by configHash+source in ExplorePreview, and configHash is computed from buildExploreCacheIdentity, which already snapshots the full upstream topology (each upstream node's id/type/label/nodeType/data-affecting config plus the connecting edges). Any structural change that affects the explore result already changes configHash, so the stored structuralVersion conveys nothing the hash does not. It is write-only redundant state (unlike previews/columns, which genuinely compare structuralVersion against useGraphStore). Removing the field from CachedExploreResult/ActiveExploreJob and the startExploreJob signature (and the three call sites in ExplorePreview.tsx) simplifies the explore plumbing with no observable behavior change.
evidence: buildExploreCacheIdentity (frontend/src/panels/explore/cacheIdentity.ts:41-80) returns { nodeId, nodes:[{id,type,label,nodeType,config}], edges:[{id,source,target}], submodels, preamble } over the upstream closure, and configHash = hashConfig({ graph: cacheIdentity, source }) (ExplorePreview.tsx:83-86). grep for '.structuralVersion' shows reads only in useDataInputColumns / usePipelineAPI (previews & columns) — none on explore job/result objects; ExplorePreview reads structuralVersion only to PASS into startExploreJob, never to compare against a cached explore entry.
est_reduction: ~8-12 LOC (1 interface field x2, 1 param, 3 call-site args, 2 nextCached assignments)
behavior_preservation: structuralVersion on explore entries is never read, and the freshness it would represent is already captured by configHash (buildExploreCacheIdentity hashes the full upstream node/edge/config topology). Deleting it leaves configHash-based freshness, LRU trimming, and all rendered output identical.

title: Unreachable GroupedColumnsTab branch — the apiInput Columns-tab render path is dead after Bundle 3a added API_INPUT to NO_COLUMNS_TAB
description: The Columns-tab render region branches on `nodeType === NODE_TYPES.API_INPUT` to render `<GroupedColumnsTab/>` instead of `<ColumnsTab/>`. That inner branch can never execute. Reaching line 1021 requires the outer guard `activeTab === "columns" && showColumnsTab` (line 1020) to be true, and `showColumnsTab = isKnownNodeType && !isInstance && !NO_COLUMNS_TAB.has(nodeType)` (line 666). Since `NO_COLUMNS_TAB` explicitly contains `NODE_TYPES.API_INPUT` (line 73), `showColumnsTab` is always `false` when `nodeType === API_INPUT`, so the API_INPUT ternary arm at 1021-1027 is unreachable. This is the exact leftover of the Bundle 3a change documented in the file's own comment (lines 61-71): API_INPUT was deliberately added to NO_COLUMNS_TAB to remove the legacy Columns tab + GroupedColumnsTab write path for apiInput, but the `nodeType === API_INPUT ? <GroupedColumnsTab .../> : <ColumnsTab .../>` ternary was not collapsed. As a consequence the `GroupedColumnsTab` import (line 25) is now used only inside dead code within this file.
evidence: Line 73: NO_COLUMNS_TAB = new Set([NODE_TYPES.API_INPUT, ...]). Line 666: showColumnsTab = isKnownNodeType && !isInstance && !NO_COLUMNS_TAB.has(nodeType) -> false for API_INPUT. Line 1020: `{activeTab === "columns" && showColumnsTab ? (` gates entry. Line 1021: `nodeType === NODE_TYPES.API_INPUT ? (<GroupedColumnsTab .../>) : (<ColumnsTab .../>)` — the true arm is statically unreachable because entering the block proves showColumnsTab===true => nodeType !== API_INPUT. Confirmed apiInputBundle3aContract.test.tsx asserts the columns button is NOT rendered for apiInput (queryByRole 'columns' -> null), and no test renders GroupedColumnsTab through NodePanel. grep confirms GroupedColumnsTab appears in NodePanel.tsx only at the import (25), the explanatory comment (65), and the dead JSX arm (1022).
est_reduction: ~9 LOC (collapse the ternary at 1020-1036 to render <ColumnsTab/> directly, and drop the now-unused GroupedColumnsTab import at line 25)
behavior_preservation: Removing the unreachable API_INPUT arm and rendering <ColumnsTab/> directly is behavior-preserving: the arm never runs for any node type (API_INPUT can never reach showColumnsTab===true), so no rendered output changes for any node. The GroupedColumnsTab import becomes unused once the arm is deleted; GroupedColumnsTab is still imported/used by its own module and other call sites, so only the NodePanel import line is removed.

title: PreviewNodeResponse redundantly re-declares six fields already inherited from NodeResult
description: PreviewNodeResponse `extends NodeResult`, and NodeResult (types.ts:138-144) already declares `timings?`, `memory?`, `node_statuses?`, `node_columns?`, `node_available_columns?`, and `node_schema_warnings?` with the exact same types and optionality. PreviewNodeResponse (types.ts:169-174) re-declares all six identically. Only `node_id: string` (line 168) is a genuine addition. The six redeclared lines are pure noise: TypeScript interface inheritance already supplies them with identical types, so removing them changes the resolved type of PreviewNodeResponse not at all. The duplication also creates a maintenance hazard — a future edit to one of these fields on NodeResult (e.g. tightening `node_columns` value type) would be silently shadowed by the stale identical copy here rather than flagged, masking the drift.
evidence: NodeResult declares (138-144): `timings?: NodeTiming[]`, `memory?: NodeMemory[]`, `node_statuses?: Record<string,string>`, `node_columns?: Record<string,ColumnInfo[]>`, `node_available_columns?: Record<string,ColumnInfo[]>`, `node_schema_warnings?: Record<string,SchemaWarning[]>`. PreviewNodeResponse `extends NodeResult` then re-declares the identical six (169-174). Backend confirms the split is the other way round: schemas.py NodeResult (229-245) does NOT carry these graph-wide fields; only PreviewNodeResponse (273-288) adds node_id + timings/memory/node_* + execution_metrics. The TS NodeResult deliberately widens (load-bearing: usePipelineAPI.ts:98-101,133-136 reads r.timings/r.memory/r.node_columns/r.node_available_columns/r.node_schema_warnings/r.execution_metrics off a NodeResult-typed param), so the fix is to drop the six redundant redeclarations from PreviewNodeResponse and keep only `node_id`.
est_reduction: 6 lines (types.ts:169-174)
behavior_preservation: Behavior-preserving: the six fields are inherited from NodeResult with byte-identical types and optionality, so the resolved shape of PreviewNodeResponse is unchanged. No runtime code; type-checking result is identical.

title: Unreachable `|| ...` fallbacks on tableStatuses lookups (one re-runs O(n) status)
description: `tableStatuses = tables.map((candidate, idx) => ratingTableStatus(candidate, idx, tables))` (line 218) has exactly one entry per table. `safeIdx = Math.min(activeTab, tables.length - 1)` is always a valid in-range index because `normaliseRatingTables(config)` is guaranteed to return at least one table (it returns `[defaultRatingTable(0)]` when `config.tables` is empty/non-array). Therefore `tableStatuses[safeIdx]` (line 219) and `tableStatuses[idx]` (line 226, where `idx` comes from the same `tables.map`) can never be `undefined`. Both `|| { state: 'problem', issues: [] }` and `|| ratingTableStatus(candidate, idx, tables)` branches are dead. The line-226 fallback is also a latent inefficiency: were it ever reachable it would recompute a full O(n) `ratingTableStatus` (which itself scans all tables for duplicate output columns) for every visible row, turning the list render into O(n^2).
evidence: Line 218 `tableStatuses = tables.map((c, idx) => ratingTableStatus(c, idx, tables))` → length === tables.length. Line 216 `safeIdx = Math.min(activeTab, tables.length - 1)` ∈ [0, length-1] given length ≥ 1 (normaliseRatingTables, ratingTableUtils.ts:50-54, always returns ≥1). So `tableStatuses[safeIdx]` and `tableStatuses[idx]` are always defined; the `|| ...` arms are never evaluated.
est_reduction: ~2 lines simplified (drop both fallbacks); removes a hidden O(n^2) trap
behavior_preservation: Behaviour-identical: the fallbacks are provably unreachable, so removing them cannot change rendered output, statuses, or filtering.
n/a
title: Editing any table silently drops a table's `onMissing` policy via the normalise→commit round-trip
description: The editor reads tables with `normaliseRatingTables(config)` and writes them back with `commitTables`/`updateTable` (`onUpdate('tables', next)`), where `next` is always reconstructed by `normaliseRatingTable` (ratingTableUtils.ts:29-48). That reconstruction keeps only {name, factors, outputColumn, defaultValue, entries} and omits `onMissing`. The backend treats `onMissing: "neutral"` as a meaningful, supported per-table miss policy (_rating.py:403-414 `_normalise_on_missing`, :515 `table.get('onMissing')`, and it is set programmatically on optimiser tables in _builders.py:1620). So if a rating-step table carries `onMissing: "neutral"` in its config and the user edits ANY field of ANY table in this editor (factors, output column, default, a single entry — all funnel through `commitTables(tables.map(...))`), every table in the array is rewritten without `onMissing`, reverting it to the default "error" policy and changing runtime semantics (a previously-tolerated miss now raises RatingTableMissError). Confidence is low because the same field is also dropped by the codegen emitter for user-authored tables (_codegen_builders.py:740-748 omits onMissing), so the canonical generated-Python form may not surface it for hand-authored tables in the first place; the editor is nonetheless a second, user-triggered strip point and has no UI to view or preserve the field.
evidence: RatingStepEditor: `tables = normaliseRatingTables(config)` (line 196); `updateTable`/`commitTables` write `tables.map(...)` back via `onUpdate('tables', next)` (lines 298-303). `normaliseRatingTable` (ratingTableUtils.ts:35-47) returns an object literal with no `onMissing` key. Backend reads it: `_rating.py:515 on_missing = _normalise_on_missing(table.get('onMissing'))`; default is "error" (_rating.py:405-409). `addTable` (line 332-333) likewise never sets it.
est_reduction: n/a

title: Cache button enabled for emit-true tables with zero selected columns — build 'succeeds' but preview can never load
description: The cache-disable gate keys only on `t.emit` (`hasEmitTrue = v2.tables.some((t) => t.emit)`), but the backend's single source of truth for 'this table contributes a data port' is `table_is_emitting` = `emit AND at least one selected column` (`src/haute/_json_shred.py:155-176`). The frontend already mirrors this exact predicate in `apiInputPorts.ts` (`emitTables`/`hasSelectedColumn`, which the docstrings call the canonical mirror), but the editor does NOT use it here — it re-derives a weaker gate. Consequence: a schema with an emit-true table but no selected columns (e.g. immediately after clicking 'Add Table', which creates `emit:true, columns:[]`, or after the user unticks every column) enables the cache button. `build_per_port_cache` then computes `emit_tables = []`, writes a meta.json with empty tables, and the build returns success (the button flips to 'Refresh Cache'). But `load_v2_api_source` raises RuntimeError on the very next preview/run: 'API Input has emit-true tables but none has any selected columns…' (`_json_shred.py:1006-1013`). The `disabledReason` text is also wrong — 'Toggle at least one table's emit so it produces a port' — emit alone does NOT produce a port.
evidence: Editor gate: line 397 `const hasEmitTrue = v2.tables.some((t) => t.emit)` → line 398 `cacheDisabled = !hasSchemaSource || !hasEmitTrue`. Backend port predicate (`_json_shred.py:158`): 'emitting = emit AND at least one selected column'; build skips parquets for emit-true zero-selected tables (`build_per_port_cache` filters with `table_is_emitting`, lines 813-821) yet still returns a success summary; load rejects (`_json_shred.py:1006-1013`). Frontend mirror that SHOULD be reused: `apiInputPorts.ts:50-66` (`emitTables` requires `hasSelectedColumn`).

title: Cache status display goes stale after an in-memory schema edit because resourceKey omits the volatile schema
description: `JsonCacheButton` builds `resourceKey = dataPath + '::' + (configPath ?? '')` and passes it to `CacheFetchButton`, whose status `useEffect` re-runs ONLY when `resourceKey` changes (deps `[resourceKey]`, with an explicit exhaustive-deps disable that excludes the `getStatus` callback). The status check sends `volatile_schema` to `getJsonCacheStatusForSchema`, and the backend validates cache freshness against that schema's fingerprint. But editing the in-memory v2 (toggling a column's `selected`, adding/removing a column, changing a column type, toggling emit) changes `volatileSchema` WITHOUT changing `resourceKey`, so the status effect never re-fires. The button keeps showing 'Refresh Cache' plus the previous schema's row/col/size stats — implying a valid cache exists for the schema the user is now looking at — when the cache is actually stale for the edited schema (the 'Not cached yet' hint likewise won't reappear). This contradicts the stated working-principle-4 intent ('the build uses what the user is looking at') for the status surface. The build itself is unaffected (doFetch captures the live volatileSchema at click time); only the cached/not-cached badge and stats are stale until the user clicks or deletes.
evidence: Line 98 `resourceKey={dataPath + "::" + (configPath ?? "")}` — no schema component. `CacheFetchButton.tsx:108-128` status effect deps `[resourceKey]` with `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps -- stable callback props`; the inline `getStatus` (ApiInputEditor lines 99-107) forwards `volatile_schema: volatileSchema` but a new closure identity does not re-run the effect. Backend status freshness is schema-fingerprint-dependent (status route calls into `is_per_port_cache_valid`, which keys on the v2 fingerprint).

title: Export-tab "Result detail" is point-specific but only reset on jobId change, so it goes stale (and keeps Save/Log disabled) after selecting a different frontier point
description: handleLoadResultDetail issues applyOptimiser with `point_index: selectedIdx` (L327), making the loaded ApplyOptimiserResponse specific to the currently selected frontier point. ResultDetailStatus then renders that point's row counts ("{returnedRows} of {totalRows} rows loaded", L810-822). But resultDetail is reset to idle ONLY when jobId changes (effect at L185-188 with deps [abortResultDetailRequest, jobId]); there is no reset when selectedIdx changes. So: load detail for point A (status becomes 'loaded'), then click point B (same job, so no reset) -> the Export tab still shows point A's row counts, attributed to the now-selected point B. Compounding this, terminalDetailBlocksActions = resultDetail.status === 'loading' || 'loaded' (L169) is passed as terminalActionsDisabled to both ExportTab (L465) and the Frontier DetailCard (L427); since 'loaded' is a persistent state never cleared on selection change, the Save Result and Log to MLflow buttons stay disabled across point selections (and effectively until the next jobId / 'Refresh detail') even though the user is now looking at a different, un-previewed point.
evidence: L327 payload: ...(selectedIdx != null && frontier ? { point_index: selectedIdx } : {}) -> detail is per-point. Reset effect L185: useEffect(() => { abortResultDetailRequest(); setResultDetail({status:'idle'}) }, [abortResultDetailRequest, jobId]) — jobId only, not selectedIdx. ResultDetailStatus L810-812 reads detail.data.preview_row_count/row_count of the OLD point. L169 terminalDetailBlocksActions includes status==='loaded'; wired to DetailCard.terminalActionsDisabled (L427) and ExportTab (L465) which disable Save/Log (DetailCard L113/L185/L199, ExportTab L719/L741). grep confirms setResultDetail only fires at L187 (jobId), L322, L332, L336 — nothing on selectedIdx. No test pins this.

location: frontend/src/panels/OptimiserPreview.tsx:151, 180, 185-199 (xConstraintIdx / actionMsg state vs. per-job reset effects); enabled by frontend/src/App.tsx:615-620 (no key on <OptimiserPreview>)
title: On job/node change the component scrubs resultDetail and ratesDetail but not actionMsg or xConstraintIdx, leaking the previous node's success message and X-axis selection between optimiser nodes
description: App.tsx renders <OptimiserPreview> inside an unkeyed IIFE (L615-620, no key={activeNodeId}); both optimiser nodes hit the same `optPreview` JSX position, so switching the active node from optimiser A to optimiser B reuses the same component instance and preserves all useState. OptimiserPreview compensates by resetting some per-job state on jobId change (L185-188 resultDetail, L196-199 ratesDetail), but it never resets actionMsg or xConstraintIdx. actionMsg is cleared only by the [selectedIdx] effect (L180) and inside the save/log handlers. Therefore: on node A click Save -> actionMsg='Saved to output/optimiser_a.json'; switch to node B; if B's selectedPointIndex equals A's (very commonly both null, so the [selectedIdx] effect does not fire), node B's panel displays node A's stale success toast referencing the wrong file/node. Similarly xConstraintIdx (L151, default 0) carries A's X-axis pick into B; FrontierTab's `constraintNames[xConstraintIdx] ?? constraintNames[0]` (L529) silently shows a non-default axis (or, if out of range, falls back to the first) for B.
evidence: App.tsx L615-620: <OptimiserPreview data={optPreview} nodeId={activeNodeId!} .../> with no key; wrapper IIFE at L585 keyed by nothing. OptimiserPreview jobId effects reset only resultDetail (L185) and ratesDetail (L196-199). actionMsg reset sites (grep): L180 [selectedIdx], L284 handleSave, L302 handleLogMlflow — none on jobId. xConstraintIdx (L151) has no reset anywhere. selectedIdx for two different nodes is frequently identical (null), so the [selectedIdx]-keyed clear is skipped, leaving A's actionMsg visible under B.

location: frontend/src/panels/OptimiserPreview.tsx:294-295, 311-312, 335 (handleSave / handleLogMlflow / handleLoadResultDetail error branches) vs. errorDetail helper L78-84
title: Terminal action error handlers drop the structured ApiError.detail that the module's own errorDetail() helper surfaces, showing only "HTTP 4xx" instead of the backend reason
description: API calls reject with ApiError whose message is just `HTTP ${status}` and whose human-readable cause lives in `.detail` (client.ts ApiError L126-138, thrown at client.ts L394). This file already defines errorDetail(error) (L78-84) which extracts a non-empty `.detail` and is used in the rates-materialisation catch (L249). But handleSave builds `Save failed: ${e}` (L295) and handleLogMlflow builds `MLflow log failed: ${e}` (L312), which stringify the ApiError via toString() to 'ApiError: HTTP 422', and handleLoadResultDetail uses `e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)` (L335) yielding 'HTTP 422' — all three discard the actual backend detail. The result is that save/log/detail failures show an opaque status code instead of the real error, contrary to the codebase's 'fail loudly with the real cause' guidance, and inconsistent with the rates path in the very same component.
evidence: client.ts: ApiError(message=`HTTP ${res.status}`, status, detail, rawDetail) constructed at client.ts:394; ApiError.detail holds the message. errorDetail (OptimiserPreview L79-83) returns `.detail` when present, used at L249 (rates catch). handleSave L295 `Save failed: ${e}` and handleLogMlflow L312 `MLflow log failed: ${e}` rely on Error.toString() -> 'ApiError: HTTP 422'; handleLoadResultDetail L335 uses e.message -> 'HTTP 422'. None call errorDetail(e), so the structured `.detail` reason is lost.

title: Downstream preview cascade mixes submodel edges with parent-graph nodes, so the cascade is silently dead when a node inside an opened submodel changes columns
description: Inside fetchPreviewImmediate the cascade builds its adjacency from graphRef.current.edges but resolves its node set from resolveGraphFromRefs(...).nodes. When a submodel is drilled in, graphRef.current holds the SUBMODEL canvas (nodes+edges) while parentGraphRef.current is set, so resolveGraphFromRefs returns the PARENT graph's nodes. propagate therefore walks submodel edge IDs to compute reachableNodeIds, but drainReadyQueue looks those submodel child IDs up in cascadeNodes (= parent nodes) via cascadeNodes.find(n => n.id === nodeId). The lookup misses every time, so each downstream child hits the `if (!dsNode || !canPreviewNode(dsNode)) { settleNode(nodeId, false); continue }` branch and the cascade no-ops: downstream nodes inside a submodel never get re-previewed (their _columns / requestedPreviewColumns are not refreshed) after an upstream column change. At the top level parentGraphRef.current is null so resolveGraphFromRefs returns graphRef.current.edges/nodes and the two sources coincide — the defect is submodel-specific.
evidence: Line 318 `const graph = resolveGraphFromRefs(graphRef, parentGraphRef, submodelsRef, preambleRef)` then line 319 `let cascadeNodes = graph.nodes`; resolveGraphFromRefs (buildGraph.ts:31-33) returns parentGraphRef.current.nodes/edges when parentGraphRef.current != null. propagate line 332 `const { edges } = graphRef.current` builds childrenBySource from the SUBMODEL edges; BFS at 346-353 yields submodel node IDs in reachableNodeIds. drainReadyQueue line 439 `const dsNode = cascadeNodes.find((n) => n.id === nodeId)` searches PARENT nodes → undefined → line 440-442 `if (!dsNode || !canPreviewNode(dsNode)) { settleNode(nodeId, false); continue }`. useSubmodelNavigation.handleDrillIntoSubmodel sets parentGraphRef.current to the parent while setNodesRaw/setEdgesRaw load the submodel into graphRef; useEdgeHandlers.onNodeClick (useEdgeHandlers.ts:351) calls fetchPreview unconditionally for nodes inside the submodel, so the path is reachable.

title: Sync-banner close button renders mojibake "â€¢" instead of an ✕ icon (double-encoded character on disk)
description: The dismiss button for the WebSocket sync-error banner has its label corrupted on disk. The on-disk bytes are `C3 A2 C5 93 E2 80 A2`, which is the UTF-8 encoding of three code points U+00E2 (â) U+0153 (œ) U+2022 (•) — i.e. the literal string "â€¢". This is a classic double-encoding of the intended close glyph U+2715 (✕, MULTIPLICATION X, correct UTF-8 `E2 9C 95`): the original `E2 9C 95` was decoded as Windows-1252 (E2→â, 9C→œ, 95→•) and re-saved as UTF-8. The button therefore displays the garbage string "â€¢" to the user rather than a close icon, in a banner that appears precisely when sync has failed (a stressful, visible moment). The directly-above sessionExpired banner uses a text "Reload" button and is unaffected, so only this control is broken — meaning the regression is easy to miss in review since the surrounding chrome looks fine.
evidence: PowerShell byte dump of the JSX text node between `opacity-100">` and `</button>` on line 537 returns raw hex `C3 A2 C5 93 E2 80 A2`; UTF-8 decode = U+00E2 U+0153 U+2022. A full-file scan found this is the ONLY mojibake occurrence outside of code comments (NON_COMMENT_COUNT=1). `text.Contains(U+2715)` is False, confirming the intended ✕ glyph is absent. Contrast lines 332/337/357 which contain a correct em-dash (U+2014), proving the file mixes good and corrupted multibyte sequences.
behavior_preservation: n/a

title: Active-node id and preview-gating logic duplicated three times instead of reusing activePanelNodeId / previewForActiveNode
description: The component already computes `const activePanelNodeId = selectedNode?.id ?? lastSelectedId` at line 235 and has a canonical helper `previewForActiveNode(previewData, activeNodeId)` (imported line 60, used line 587) that returns the preview only when `previewData.nodeId === activeNodeId`. Yet the DataPreview IIFE recomputes the identical expression `const activeNodeId = selectedNode?.id ?? lastSelectedId` at line 586, and the NodePanel prop block hand-reimplements the same node-id match twice more: `previewData?.nodeId === activePanelNodeId ? previewData?.error_line ?? null : null` (699-700) and `previewData?.status === "ok" && previewData?.nodeId === activePanelNodeId ? previewData.preview : undefined` (703-707). These open-code the exact gate that `previewForActiveNode` encapsulates. Consolidating to one `activePanelNodeId` value and deriving `const activePreview = previewForActiveNode(previewData, activePanelNodeId)` once, then reading `activePreview?.error_line` / `activePreview?.preview`, removes the redundant local and the two inline reimplementations, eliminating the risk that one of the three copies drifts from the helper.
evidence: Line 235: `const activePanelNodeId = selectedNode?.id ?? lastSelectedId`. Line 586 (inside DataPreview IIFE): `const activeNodeId = selectedNode?.id ?? lastSelectedId` — byte-identical RHS. Lines 699-707 inline-test `previewData?.nodeId === activePanelNodeId` twice, duplicating activePreview.ts:8 `return previewData.nodeId === activeNodeId ? previewData : null`.
est_reduction: ~8-12 lines; collapses 1 redundant local + 2 inline reimplementations into 1 reuse of the existing helper
behavior_preservation: Behavior-preserving: `activeNodeId` (586) and `activePanelNodeId` (235) evaluate to the same value every render; the inline `nodeId === activePanelNodeId` checks return the same error_line/preview as `previewForActiveNode(previewData, activePanelNodeId)?.error_line / .preview` (the helper additionally guards null previewData/null id, which the `?.` chains already handle).

title: closePanel clears previewData but does not cancelPreview, leaving an in-flight backend request running and previewBusy stuck true after a full panel close
description: closePanel() fully tears down the selection (setSelectedNode(null), lastSelectedNodeRef=null, setLastSelectedId(null), setPreviewDataRef.current(null)) but never calls cancelPreview(). If a preview fetch is in flight when the user closes the panel via onPaneClick (line 561 → closePanel), the request's seq is not invalidated and `requestStillCurrent()` stays true, so fetchPreviewImmediate's `.then` still runs setPreviewData(preview) (usePipelineAPI.ts:529) and setPreviewBusy(false) only fires when the network round-trip eventually settles. Because the panel is closed, activePanelNodeId is null and previewForActiveNode gates the repainted data out of view, so there is no visual corruption — but the backend preview keeps executing to completion (wasted compute, and any downstream cascade in propagate() keeps writing _columns into nodes via setNodesRaw at 463/539), and previewBusy remains true in the meantime. This is asymmetric with handleDeleteNode/handleSwapEdgeJoinInputs which deliberately call cancelPreview(), and with the keyboard-shortcut closePanel path. Confidence is low because no user-visible artifact results and the request aborts naturally once it finishes; flagged as a resource/robustness gap, not a display defect.
evidence: closePanel (200-208) dependency list `[setUtilityOpen, setImportsOpen, setGitOpen]` and body contain no cancelPreview call, while handleSwapEdgeJoinInputs (447) and useEdgeHandlers.onNodeClick (344) both call cancelPreview() before/around selection changes. cancelPreview (usePipelineAPI.ts:609-618) is what bumps previewRequestSeq + aborts the controller; without it the in-flight `.then` at usePipelineAPI.ts:508/529 still treats itself as current.
behavior_preservation: n/a

title: Position-only dirty derivation's never-saved branch ignores edges/preamble (latent divergence from computeDirty)
description: For the lastSavedSnapshot===null case, computeDirty returns `persistedFingerprint !== EMPTY_SNAPSHOT` (dirty if ANY of nodes/edges/preamble is non-empty), but the position-only sibling computeDirtyForPositionOnlyNodes returns `nodes.length > 0` only. On a never-saved workspace with zero nodes but non-empty edges or a non-empty preamble, these two disagree: computeDirty says dirty, computeDirtyForPositionOnlyNodes says clean. The two functions are meant to be drop-in equivalents for the position-only fast path. The divergence is currently UNREACHABLE because hasOnlyNodePositionChanges() (the only gate to this branch) returns false whenever both node arrays are empty (its per-index loop never runs, so positionChanged stays false), so setNodesRaw never reaches the position-only branch with nodes.length===0. It is therefore a dormant correctness inconsistency rather than an active bug, but it is a real trap for any future caller/refactor that reuses computeDirtyForPositionOnlyNodes or changes the gating predicate.
evidence: computeDirty null-branch (line 360): `selectIsDirty({lastSavedSnapshot:null}, persistedFingerprint)` => `persistedFingerprint !== EMPTY_SNAPSHOT` where EMPTY_SNAPSHOT = serialize({nodes:[],edges:[],preamble:''}). computeDirtyForPositionOnlyNodes null-branch (line 385): `return nodes.length > 0` — only inspects nodes, never edges or preamble. selectIsDirty/EMPTY_SNAPSHOT defined in utils/graphSnapshot.ts:121,133-141. Unreachability: hasOnlyNodePositionChanges (228-253) returns `positionChanged` initialized false; for empty arrays the loop body is skipped so it returns false, so setNodesRaw (530) never enters the position-only branch when nodes is empty.
behavior_preservation: n/a (bug)

title: Three change-classification helpers duplicate the same key-diff skeleton
description: The three setNodesRaw/setEdgesRaw change classifiers share one verbatim skeleton: length guard -> per-index loop -> `previous === node` bail -> id-equality bail -> build `new Set([...Object.keys(previous), ...Object.keys(node)])` -> for each key, if it is a managed UI field record a `changed` flag via !Object.is(...), else require Object.is(prevValue,nextValue) and bail false otherwise -> finally return `changed`. They diverge only in which fields are 'tracked' vs 'bail': hasOnlyNodeUiFieldChanges treats position as an extra bail and data-ref as a bail; hasOnlyNodePositionChanges treats position as the tracked delta and UI fields as ignorable; hasOnlyEdgeUiFieldChanges drops position/data entirely. This is incidental duplication (~85 LOC) distinct from the already-known SIMP-02 (which targets the mutators' fingerprint/version bookkeeping, not these classifiers). Note this is a marginal cleanup: the per-helper divergence in tracked-vs-bail field roles means a unified helper would need a small config object, so the readability win is modest.
evidence: hasOnlyNodeUiFieldChanges (196-226), hasOnlyNodePositionChanges (228-253) and hasOnlyEdgeUiFieldChanges (255-281) all contain the identical `const keys = new Set([...Object.keys(previous), ...Object.keys(node/edge)]); for (const key of keys) {... if (UI_FIELDS.has(key)) { if(!Object.is(prev[key],next[key])) changed=true; continue } if (!Object.is(prev[key],next[key])) return false }` block; the node variants additionally early-bail on `previous.data !== node.data` and `!positionsEqual(...)`. REACT_FLOW_NODE_UI_FIELDS (178-185) / REACT_FLOW_EDGE_UI_FIELDS (187) parameterize the only set difference.
est_reduction: ~25-35 LOC if unified behind a single classifyFieldChanges(prev,next,{uiFields,extraBail,tracked}) helper
behavior_preservation: A shared classifier driven by the per-call field-role config produces identical boolean results: same length/identity/id guards, same Object.is comparisons, same UI-vs-structural partition; only the extraction site moves. No observable change to setNodesRaw/setEdgesRaw outputs.

title: window.open(..., "_blank") omits noopener — reverse tabnabbing
description: handleSubmit opens the compare/PR URL with window.open(result.compare_url, "_blank") but does not pass "noopener,noreferrer". The newly opened tab receives a live window.opener reference and can navigate the originating app tab (reverse tabnabbing) and read the referrer. This is the only window.open in the frontend so there is no shared safe helper establishing a pattern; the two-arg form is the unguarded default.
evidence: Line 137-141: `const result = await gitSubmit(); if (result.compare_url) { window.open(result.compare_url, "_blank") }`. No third feature-string argument, so window.opener is non-null in the opened tab. compare_url is built backend-side from the remote origin (src/haute/_git.py:284 _build_compare_url) for github/gitlab/azure/bitbucket; a malicious or compromised remote URL would be opened with opener access. Fix: window.open(url, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer") or set the returned handle's .opener = null.

title: Submit succeeds silently with no feedback when compare_url is null
description: handleSubmit only opens a URL when result.compare_url is truthy and otherwise gives the user no confirmation at all (no toast, no banner, no 'submitted' state). The backend submit_for_review returns HTTP 200 with compare_url=null for unrecognised/self-hosted git hosts and when there is no remote (src/haute/_git.py:309-310 returns None for unknown hosts; _build_compare_url returns None when there is no remote). In those deployments a successful 'Submit for review' click pushes the branch but the panel only refreshes — the user has no way to tell whether anything happened or where to open the PR.
evidence: Line 138-141: `if (result.compare_url) { window.open(result.compare_url, "_blank") } await refresh()`. The else branch (compare_url === null) does nothing. submit_for_review (src/haute/_git.py:837-869) sets push success but compare_url can be None, and the response still resolves (no throw), so the catch block is not entered and no success indication is shown.

title: Branch dropdown renders an empty box when no group has entries
description: The dropdown body is four conditionally-rendered sections (protected / yours / others / archived), each guarded by `<group>.length > 0`. There is no fallback when all four are empty (e.g. branches is still [] before listGitBranches resolves, or a repo that exposes only the current non-protected branch which is filtered out of every group). In that case opening the dropdown shows a bordered, shadowed but completely empty popover with no 'No branches' message, which reads as a broken control.
evidence: Lines 325, 334, 348, 362 each gate on `*.length > 0`; the enclosing `branchDropdownOpen && (<div>...)` at line 322 has no else/empty-state child. If branches === [] then protectedBranches/yourBranches/otherBranches/archivedBranches are all [] (lines 216-219) and the popover div at 323 contains nothing.

title: Protected branch-name list duplicated across filter expressions
description: The literal ["main", "master", "develop"] is written twice in the derived-state block (otherBranches exclusion at line 217 and protectedBranches definition at line 219) and the same concept is hand-maintained against the backend's protected-branch set. Duplicating the literal risks drift (one filter updated, the other not), and the two filters are computed by re-scanning `branches` independently. Extract a single `const PROTECTED = new Set(["main", "master", "develop"])` (module-level constant) and reference it in both filters.
evidence: Line 217: `otherBranches = branches.filter((b) => !b.is_yours && !b.is_archived && !["main", "master", "develop"].includes(b.name))`; line 219: `protectedBranches = branches.filter((b) => ["main", "master", "develop"].includes(b.name))`. Same array literal in two places.
est_reduction: ~2 lines net plus removal of a drift hazard
behavior_preservation: Pure refactor: identical membership test via a shared Set/array; output of both filters unchanged.

title: Conditional-mode a11y "sentinel" IIFE renders a no-op element invisible to every user and unverified by any test
description: In the conditional render path, an 18-line IIFE conditionally emits a <span className="result-value accent" data-accent ... aria-hidden="true" style={{position:'absolute',width:1,height:1,overflow:'hidden',clip:'rect(0,0,0,0)'}} />. The element is simultaneously visually hidden (1px clip-rect) AND removed from the accessibility tree (aria-hidden="true"), so it conveys nothing to sighted users or screen-reader users. It is also never asserted by any test in the conditional context. When the component is rendered framed (frame=true), TraceCalculationFrame (TraceDetail.tsx:73-92) ALREADY renders the result as <span className="result-value accent" data-accent data-testid="trace-calculation-result"> whenever result is defined, so the sentinel is redundant; when rendered unframed (frame=false, the way StepCard.tsx:230-240 always invokes it) the sentinel is the only such element but, being aria-hidden + clipped, it still surfaces nothing. The whole IIFE — including the branchTexts join, the resultInBranch substring test, and the early `return null` 'not applicable' path the test comment defends — can be deleted with no observable behaviour change.
evidence: CalculationHero.tsx:512-530 builds `branchTexts = branches.map(b=>b.result??"").join(" ")`, `resultInBranch = branchTexts.includes(resultStr)`, and only when true returns a span with aria-hidden="true" and clip:rect(0,0,0,0). Grep over frontend/src/**/*.test.* for data-accent/data-muted/result-value shows only CalculationHero.test.tsx:115 and :511, both exercising the ARITHMETIC default (no conditional sentinel rendered); the matched element there is the frame's own result-value span from TraceDetail.tsx:75. errorUI test F (calculationHero.errorUI.test.tsx:237-273) only asserts the sentinel's ABSENCE indirectly (no alert) for the not-found case. Hence nothing relies on the sentinel's presence.
est_reduction: ~19 LOC (lines 512-530)
behavior_preservation: The emitted element is aria-hidden and 1px-clipped, so it is invisible to AT and sighted users alike; no test queries it in the conditional path; the framed result element from TraceCalculationFrame is unaffected. Deleting the IIFE leaves the rendered/queryable DOM unchanged for every covered case.

title: Conditional branch matching indexes substituted-text branches by the expression-text branch index, assuming the two independent parses are positionally aligned
description: `branches = parseBranches(expression.expression_text)` and `subBranches = parseBranches(calculation.substituted_text)` are parsed independently, then `isBranchMatched(idx)` reads `subBranches[idx]` using an index derived from iterating `branches` (line 481 `branches.map((branch, idx) => ...)`, line 472 `branches.some((b,i)=>...isBranchMatched(i))`). This is only correct if both strings parse into the same number of branches in the same order. They can diverge: (a) any of the known parseBranches mis-splits (a then/otherwise value containing the word 'when'/'otherwise') affects expression_text and substituted_text differently because their tokens differ, shifting the index mapping; (b) the backend's substituted_text can legitimately have a different branch shape (e.g. a pre-resolved or collapsed branch) than the raw expression_text. When they misalign, `subBranches[idx]` is the wrong branch, so `isBranchMatched` consults the wrong substituted result and the highlighted branch is wrong. This only bites when the backend does NOT supply taken_branch_index (line 461-463 backendTakenBranchIndex===null), i.e. the legacy fallback path; when taken_branch_index is present the index is used directly (line 482-486) and isBranchMatched is bypassed.
evidence: Line 459 `const subBranches = parseBranches(calculation.substituted_text)`; line 470-473 `function isBranchMatched(idx){ const sub = subBranches[idx]; if(!sub?.result) return false; return sub.result.includes(resultStr) }`; line 475-477 `branches.some((b,i)=>!b.isOtherwise && isBranchMatched(i))`; line 481-486 maps over `branches` and, when backendTakenBranchIndex===null, calls `isBranchMatched(idx)` with the branches-index. No code aligns subBranches to branches by condition/position before indexing.

title: parseBranches silently drops all text preceding an `otherwise` clause when no when/then pair is present
description: After the when/then loop, parseBranches runs `text.slice(lastIndex).match(/otherwise\s+(.+)/i)` and, on a match, pushes a single otherwise branch. If the text contains `otherwise` but ZERO well-formed `when ... then ...` pairs, the loop makes no iterations (lastIndex stays 0), the otherwise-match captures only the text AFTER `otherwise`, and a branch is pushed — making branches.length === 1, which suppresses the `branches.length === 0` fallback that would otherwise have preserved the full text. The leading text before `otherwise` is therefore silently discarded. This is a distinct edge from the documented 'then-value contains when' mis-split: it is the no-when/then-at-all case. In practice conditionals always begin with `when`, so reachability is low, but the function is a general string parser and the discard is silent (no loud failure), violating the repo's 'fail loudly' preference.
evidence: Line 80-87 while-loop produces 0 matches for input like "foo otherwise bar" (no `then`); line 89 `text.slice(0).match(/otherwise\s+(.+)/i)` captures "bar"; line 90-95 pushes {result:"bar", isOtherwise:true}; line 97-99 `if (branches.length === 0)` is now false so the raw-text fallback is skipped — "foo" is lost. Compare the clean path where text starts with `when`: the loop consumes the when/then, lastIndex lands at the ` otherwise`, and the prefix is preserved as branches.

title: Declared calculation prop field `taken_branch` is never read by CalculationHero
description: The local CalculationHeroProps.calculation interface declares `taken_branch?: string | null` (line 41), but the component only ever consumes `taken_branch_index` (line 460). `taken_branch` is read nowhere in CalculationHero.tsx. It mirrors the wider trace wire type (types/trace.ts), but on THIS component's prop surface it is dead: it can be removed from the local interface without affecting behaviour, narrowing the component's declared contract to what it actually uses. Low value; flagged for completeness.
evidence: Grep for `taken_branch\b` in frontend/src shows it consumed only in types/guards.ts and types/trace.ts (parsing) and asserted in guard/TracePanel tests; within CalculationHero.tsx the only branch-index read is line 460 `calculation.taken_branch_index ?? takenBranchIndex`. No reference to `calculation.taken_branch` exists in the component.
est_reduction: 1 line (interface field)
behavior_preservation: Field is never read in this component; removing it from the local prop interface changes no runtime behaviour and only tightens the declared type to the fields actually used.

title: "Unmatched rows" counter can go negative because match counts are summed across independently-counted (possibly overlapping) rules
description: The per-rule match counts are computed by counting, for EACH rule, every preview row that satisfies that rule independently (lines 142-168). `matchedRows` is then `matchCounts.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)` and `unmatchedCount = totalRows - matchedRows` (lines 172-173), with no clamping. When two or more continuous rules overlap, a single row is counted once per matching rule, so `matchedRows` can exceed `totalRows`, making `unmatchedCount` negative. The Default counter at line 554 then renders e.g. "-2 of 100 rows". Overlapping continuous rules are an explicitly supported and merely warned-about state (see warnings block lines 193-198 and detectOverlaps). The backend never double-counts: src/haute/_rating.py _apply_banding builds a when/then chain (first-match-wins, lines 119-133), so a row is assigned by exactly one rule. The preview model (count-each-rule) therefore diverges from real assignment semantics and produces an impossible negative unmatched figure.
evidence: matchCounts: rules.map(r => previewRows.filter(row => matchesContinuousRule(Number(row[column]), r)).length) counts each rule independently. matchedRows=sum(matchCounts); unmatchedCount=totalRows-matchedRows (lines 172-173). With rules [<=15 'A'] and [>=10 <=20 'B'] a row at 12 is counted by both, so two rules over 1 row => matchedRows=2 for 1 row; with totalRows=1, unmatchedCount=-1. Rendered verbatim at line 554: `{unmatchedCount} of {totalRows} rows`. Backend _rating.py assigns first-match-only, so the true unmatched is >=0.

title: Breakpoint per-row "Matches" column is misaligned because match counts are derived from sorted/filtered rules but indexed by raw row order
description: For breakpoints mode, matchCounts is built as `breakpointsToRules(bpRules, rightClosed).map(cont => count rows matching cont)` (lines 149-159). `breakpointsToRules` (bandingUtils.ts) FILTERS OUT rows with blank/non-numeric boundaries and SORTS the remaining boundaries ascending, and may APPEND an extra open-ended rule for a blank-boundary row. The resulting array length and order therefore do NOT correspond 1:1 to `factor.rules` (the raw breakpoint rows). However that same `matchCounts` array is passed to BreakpointGrid (line 488), which renders `matchCounts[i]` indexed by the raw breakpoint-row index `i` (BreakpointGrid.tsx lines 250-255, breakpoints.map((bp,i)=>...) with no sort). Whenever boundaries are entered out of order (a common transient state, also flagged by the order warning), or a blank/invalid boundary sits before a numeric one, each row's displayed Matches count belongs to a different band.
evidence: Rows [{boundary:'65'},{boundary:'25'}]: breakpointsToRules sorts to [25,65] => contRules order [<=25, (25,65]]. matchCounts=[count(<=25), count((25,65])]. BreakpointGrid row0 (boundary 65) shows matchCounts[0]=count(<=25); row1 (boundary 25) shows matchCounts[1]=count((25,65]) — both wrong. Also rows [{25},{'',senior},{65}]: bounded sorts to [25,65], blank skipped+appended last => row1 (blank) shows matchCounts[1]=count((25,65]) instead of the open-ended count. No realignment exists between the editor's sorted contRules and the grid's raw-order rendering.

title: Match counts include rules with an empty assignment that the backend silently drops
description: Match counting for categorical (lines 142-147) and continuous/breakpoints (lines 152-168) only inspects the matching predicate (value equality / interval membership) and ignores whether the rule has a non-empty `assignment`.
